candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record confirms primary Sjögren's syndrome (20-year sicca symptoms, anti-Ro positivity, ANA 1:160 nucleolar pattern, no scleroderma on biopsy) as the underlying etiology, but the benchmark reference is the composite diagnosis 'Calcinosis cutis in Sjögren syndrome.' C001 names only the parent condition and does not include calcinosis cutis, which is the biopsy-confirmed finding driving the most likely diagnosis question.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Identifies the underlying autoimmune condition (primary Sjögren's syndrome) but omits the specific complication/manifestation component (calcinosis cutis) that is the central diagnostic object requested

case_quality_flags: Calcinosis cutis is an uncommon manifestation of Sjögren syndrome; scleroderma was appropriately excluded by biopsy and clinical features, supporting the composite diagnosis.
